title: OODLC catalog file (v0)
description: One YAML file in a catalog directory. Any file may hold any of the sections: intents, outcomes, behaviors, conditions and constraints, and the inventory (actors, capabilities, experiences, unknowns), which explains the system and never blocks.

terms.description: The vocabulary: what words like order, paid or customer mean in this system. See docs/decisions/0013.

changes.description: Only in oodlc/changes/: intents to change the system, agreed before the code. See docs/decisions/0012.

status.description: Drafted, not yet approved by a human. A proposed entry runs and is reported, but never blocks. Approving it means deleting this field. See docs/decisions/0006.

headers.description: Request headers. A null value drops that header; null sends no headers at all.

db.description: Rows each table of the simulated database starts with, by table name (schema.table outside public). Listing a table replaces the rows defaults or the schema gave it. Needs database in oodlc/config.yaml.

repeat.description: Send the same request this many times against the same state (2 is a replay). The last response is observed; effects accumulate.

fuzz.description: Rewrite the request body before sending it: injection (every string becomes an attack payload), oversize (adds a 1MB field), extra-fields (adds privileged fields such as role: admin to every object).

status.description: An exact status, or a matcher such as { gte: 400, lte: 499 }

intent.description: The intent this outcome serves. An outcome traces to an intent, a confirmed capability, or both. See docs/decisions/0010.

capability.description: The capability this outcome protects. See docs/decisions/0010.

when.description: Expectations per condition. Each key is a condition from `conditions`; each field it names replaces the same field of `expect` under that condition. See docs/decisions/0004.

constraints.description: Traceability only: the constraints this outcome depends on. Every constraint is checked on every run regardless. See docs/decisions/0002.

behavior.description: Observed by the runner, not durable by default. Drift is reported, never blocking.

capability.description: The capability this behavior is part of. See docs/decisions/0010.

actor.description: Who uses the system. Part of the inventory, which never blocks. See docs/decisions/0010.

capability.description: What the system lets an actor do: 'actor can verb object'. Proposed when discovered or drafted; a person confirms it by deleting status. A confirmed capability can justify an outcome. Never blocks. See docs/decisions/0010.

surfaces.description: Triggers that reach it, e.g. POST /checkout

evidence.description: Where the claim comes from: a file, a probe, a record

experience.description: What an actor goes through across capabilities, and when it feels broken. Never blocks. See docs/decisions/0010.

steps.description: Capability ids, in the order the actor meets them

feels_broken_when.description: Failures the actor would notice. Each is a candidate condition or constraint.

evidence.description: Where the journey was seen: a capture, a trace export

unknown.description: A question the system can't answer about itself, and who can. See docs/decisions/0010.

ask.description: The role that can answer it, e.g. product owner

about.description: Ids of the entries it is about

answer.description: What a person said. An answered question is no longer open.

term.description: A word people and agents must mean the same thing by. The id is the word, singular and lowercase.

statement.description: What it means here, in a sentence

aka.description: Other words people use for the same thing

change.description: An intent to change the system, agreed before the code exists. Once merged, it lets a code pull request change exactly what it amends, inside the capabilities it reaches, and nothing it rules out. See docs/decisions/0012.

because.description: Why, in words a reviewer can argue with

reaches.description: Capabilities it may touch. Without it, only what it amends

expect.description: Merged over the outcome's expect: body fields by key, effects by kind, the rest replaced

constraint.description: Human-declared invariant. Checked on every run (outcomes, behaviors, probes of unknown routes); a violation always blocks, and so does changing or removing one.

check.description: JS expression over effects, state, response, request and db (each table's rows after the run, with the simulated database); must be true
